rounds.proof_sketch: When AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES dispatches with float32 input, T=float. Thus bias_gn[i] is type float, and static_cast<float>(float_value) is a no-op identity operation. Both expressions evaluate to the same float value with no conversion.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes a static_cast<float>() from a value that is already of type float. When the input tensor has dtype=float32, the AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES macro instantiates the kernel template with scalar_t=float, making T=float. The bias_gn pointer is const T* = const float*, so bias_gn[i] is already float. Casting float to float via static_cast produces identical machine code and identical results. This is a compile-time no-op, making the mutant semantically equivalent to the original for all float32 inputs regardless of their numerical values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed float32 contract. The only way to expose a difference would be to use float64 inputs (where T=double, and the cast would truncate precision), but the input specification fixes dtype=torch.float32.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for cast removal operators should check whether the source and target types are identical at instantiation time. For templated CUDA kernels with AT_DISPATCH macros, the effective type depends on the input dtype, so mutations involving casts from template types to concrete types should be pre-filtered as equivalent when those types match.
